title: Private deploy: early-failure probes, Terraform sanity checks, and rollback plan
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures a compact set of early-failure probes (fast checks run immediately after install or upgrade), Terraform sanity assertions to run before an apply/upgrade, and a minimal rollback plan for private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. Intended for SREs / field engineers doing upgrades or first-time installs. Focus is pragmatic: fast signals + low-risk rollback steps.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to private deployments managed with our Terraform modules and installer bundle (customer VPC + host nodes).
- Assumes access to: Terraform state backend, bastion host, kubeconfig for control-plane, and customer VPN/peering established.
- Not a complete runbook for catastrophic recovery; meant to catch the majority of common early failures within the first 30 minutes post-upgrade.

Quick smoke probes (run first, ~5–10m):
1) Control plane reachability
   - From bastion: curl -k https://CONTROL_PLANE_HOST/healthz (expect 200 and JSON {"status":"ok"} or equivalent)
   - kubectl get nodes --request-timeout=10s
2) Network basics (VPC peering, SGs, routes)
   - ping -c 3 MODEL_SERVING_IP (or curl to /live endpoint)
   - ip route show; verify route to storage, artifact registry, and redis/cache IP ranges
   - verify security groups: aws ec2 describe-security-groups --filters Name=group-name,Values="redwood-*" (ensure ports 22, 443, 1024-65535 ephemeral and model ports open)
3) Service bootstrap health
   - kubectl -n redwood get pods -o wide | egrep "CrashLoopBackOff|ImagePullBackOff|Pending" (if any found, capture pod describe + logs)
   - curl -sS http://localhost:8080/metrics | head -n 20 (check token-bucket and request-queue metrics are non-empty)
4) Storage and artifact availability
   - test download of a small model artifact: curl -I ARTIFACT_URL (expect 200/206)
   - ls -l /mnt/model-cache | wc -l (ensure cache mount is present)
5) GPU & driver sanity (if applicable)
   - nvidia-smi || /opt/nvidia/bin/nvidia-smi (check driver + cuda version)
   - dmesg | tail -n 50 (look for GPU or VFIO errors)
6) KV cache / redis connectivity
   - redis-cli -h REDIS_HOST PING (expect PONG)
   - INFO keyspace; check for large eviction counts

Terraform sanity checklist (pre-apply / pre-upgrade):
- terraform workspace show -> confirm correct workspace/environment
- terraform refresh (or plan with -refresh=true) to detect drift
- Inspect plan for any destructive changes: grep -E "-\s+module|-/resource" and manually review unexpected deletes
- Ensure remote state lock is working: terraform force-unlock should not be required. If lock appears stale, investigate CI job or operator holding lock.
- Confirm provider versions: terraform providers lock file matches expected (provider "aws" ~> 4.x, provider "kubernetes" ~> 2.x etc.)
- Check variables for critical changes: any change to network cidrs, subnets, route table attachments, or tenancy must be reviewed and avoided unless planned with downtime windows
- Run module-specific validation: 
  - terraform plan -target=module.network -out=network.plan
  - terraform show -json network.plan | jq '.resource_changes[] | select(.change.actions | index("delete"))' (quick filter for deletes)

Preflight monitoring toggles (easy to forget):
- Ensure rolling-update/eviction behaviour is configured: controller.maxUnavailable is not 100% for critical deployments
- Confirm autoscaler limits: min replicas > 0 to avoid total removal during scale tests
- Feature flags: disable new experimental routing plugin until canary passes

Common early-failure patterns and pragmatic remediation steps:
1) Pods stuck in Pending due to insufficient eni/ips or taints
   - Check node allocatable vs pod requirement (kubectl describe node)
   - If IP exhaustion: add extra node to pool or expand subnet; temporary quick fix: cordon unschedulable nodes with no pods and drain non-critical ones
2) ImagePullBackOff – registry/auth issues
   - docker pull ARTIFACT_URL from bastion to validate credentials
   - Confirm KMS/GCR/AWS ECR credential helper running; check secret exists in kube: kubectl -n redwood get secret image-pull-secret -o yaml
3) CrashLoopBackOff – config or runtime mismatch
   - kubectl logs --previous -n NAMESPACE POD; check for immediate OOM or missing env var
   - If OOM: inspect node memory pressure and QoS, adjust resource requests or increase node mem briefly
4) Certificate mismatch / TLS handshake failures (control plane or external integrations)
   - openssl s_client -connect HOST:443 -showcerts; compare CN/SAN vs expected shortname
   - Common cause: cert not yet rotated into secret post-upgrade; re-sync secret from vault or run the cert-rotation job
5) GPU driver mismatch after kernel update
   - Reboot nodes in a controlled manner with driver reinstall (documented in infra notes). If drivers fail to load, rollback kernel update or use node pool with old kernel until drivers are rebuilt
6) Terraform apply partially completes and leaves mixed state
   - Do not re-run apply blindly. Capture terraform state pull, and use terraform state list to inspect broken resources. Prefer targeted terraform apply -target for small fixes or manual repair in cloud console then import into state

Fast rollback plan (20–60 minutes objective for common regressions):
- If a config-only regression (feature flag, routing plugin): toggle feature OFF and verify traffic drops back to previous behavior (no infra change needed)
- If new release of control-plane is causing failed jobs: shift traffic to previous release by scaling back new deployment and scaling up the prior replica set (kubectl scale deployment/my-app --replicas=N)
- If Terraform changed network constructs accidentally: immediate path is to restore a known-good state file snapshot (s3/terraform-state-backups/YYYYMMDD) and re-run terraform apply against that state with the old plan (ensure state backend locking).
- For image/registry rollbacks: retag previous image to 'current' and update imagePullSecret expiry if needed; update deployment image with kubectl set image to previous digest
- Node-level rollback (kernel/driver): evacuate workloads to a warm node pool with older kernel, then scale old pool up and drain affected nodes

Example commands (targeted, safe-first):
- terraform plan -target=module.control_plane -out=cp.plan
- terraform apply cp.plan
- kubectl -n redwood rollout undo deployment/control-plane --to-revision=3
- aws s3 cp s3://tf-state-backups/private-deploy/backup-2025-06-10.tfstate ./restore.tfstate
- terraform state replace-provider 'registry.terraform.io/-/module' 'registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/module' (example of targeted state surgery)

Automation and probe script (bastion friendly):
- A short bash script we encourage engineers to run after every upgrade; keep it idempotent and timeboxed to 10 minutes.
- snippet: 
  set -euo pipefail
  echo "CONTROL plane health"; curl -fsS https://$CONTROL_PLANE/healthz || echo "control plane fail"
  kubectl get pods -n redwood --field-selector=status.phase!=Running -o wide || true
  redis-cli -h $REDIS_HOST PING || echo "redis fail"
  if command -v nvidia-smi >/dev/null 2>&1; then nvidia-smi -L || echo "gpu fail"; fi

Postmortem capture checklist (if not immediately resolved):
- Capture kubectl describe for failing pods, nodes, and statefulsets- store pod logs (kubectl logs POD --all-containers > pod.POD.logs.txt)
- Save terraform plan and state snapshot used for the change- record terraform apply logs and the exact commit/tag of the installer bundle- note exact timestamps for when behavior started and any prior config changes

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Add automated terraform preflight that fails a PR if plan includes deletion of > 2 network resources (JIRA-1729)
- Add a lightweight orchestration check that can warm the model cache before route cutover to avoid cold miss storm
- Consider a one-click rollback in console that: restores tfstate snapshot, flips feature flag, and scales previous replicas (requires work on orchestration APIs)

Notes for on-call handover:
- If you escalate, include: terraform plan output, last terraform apply logs, failing pod names, and the result of the smoke probes above.
- Link to KB and follow-up ticket template: linked_artifacts in header for quick reference.

Revision history:
- 2024-11-03: initial draft (Priya)
- 2025-02-14: added GPU driver checklist and fast rollback steps (Aaron)
- 2025-06-12: refined terraform preflight commands and added postmortem checklist (Marta)

End of doc.
